title: Offer Handling Strategy
content:
Multiple OffersMost common for at- or below-market listings
  • Having leverage is the best scenario for us.
  • We can call for highest and best by a set deadline.
  • We can negotiate directly with the best offer to reach an agreement quickly.
  • The second-best offer can serve as a backup in case the first deal falls through.
Single OfferAligns with a higher pricing strategy
  • With only one bidder, we have less leverage, so counteroffers must be strategic.
  • Focus on maximizing price and terms within the limits of our negotiating power.

Strong Offer Traits (beyond price)

Verified pre-approval from a reputable lenderCash offers (highly preferred)Appraisal guaranteeFree rent-back period if needed by the sellerWaived inspection contingency (not recommended, but sometimes used in competitive situations)

Offer Acceptance & Next Steps

Once an offer is accepted, the buyer must adhere to contract timelines. Each milestone completed increases the likelihood of a successful closing.

48 hrsEarnest money deposit — proof provided
7 daysInspection period (typical, per contract)
7 daysMortgage application submitted
30 daysMortgage approval deadline

Buyer Contingencies Allowing an Exit with Earnest Money Refund

  • Inspection period: buyer can walk away for any reason.
  • Mortgage denial: if financing is denied, the buyer can exit.
  • Low appraisal: buyer can walk; buyer & seller can renegotiate the price; or buyer can bridge the gap with additional cash (effectively an appraisal guarantee after the fact).
  • Other written contingencies: must be met or waived for the deal to proceed.
